proposer.rules:
1. A qualification bullet or sentence that names a skill counts; a job title or a
   years-of-experience line ("experience as a software engineer") does not.
2. An API being consumed is not the `apis` skill. `apis` means building or designing APIs.
3. Any required mention wins; raw_text quotes the determining mention.
4. Responsibilities do not count unless the candidate is also asked for it.
5. Do not add a broad or parent skill the text does not name.

rules:
One label per posting, or none (`null`) when no degree is mentioned.

- `degree` is the **lowest** level named: `bachelor`, `master`, `phd` — the least a
  candidate must hold to get in. "Bachelor's or Master's" → `bachelor`; "MS or PhD" →
  `master`; "Master's degree (or above)" → `master`. "Degree in …", "university degree",
  "completed studies", "currently studying" with no level → `bachelor`. When the whole
  mention is optional ("ein Master oder Ph.D. ist von Vorteil"), the level is still the
  lowest named, with `nice_to_have`. A higher level the posting also welcomes is not
  recorded: one label per posting (decision of 2026-11-19, HIR-245).
- `degree_requirement` follows the skill rule: `nice_to_have` only when marked optional;
  otherwise `required`, including a bare mention in a requirements list. Most postings
  are bare mentions, so most labeled degrees are `required` — that is correct, not a
  default to fix.
- `degree_or_equivalent` is true when the posting accepts experience in place of the degree:
  "or equivalent experience", "or comparable qualification/experience". "…or a related
  field" / "or a comparable technical focus" widens the *field*, not the requirement → false.
- `degree_signal` quotes the phrase, including the "or equivalent" wording when present.
- `attrs_reviewed: false` marks pre-filled German/degree labels not yet checked by a person.

Added 2026-11-11 (HIR-251, Chandler's yes). When the posting accepts **any one of several
skills** for one ask, each of them gets the same `alternative_group` number — 1 for the
first such set in the posting, 2 for the next. Every other criterion has no
`alternative_group`.

- **Markers:** "at least one of", "one or more of", "X, Y or Z", "X and/or Y", and examples
  offered for a single ask ("a language such as X, Y or Z", "a framework like X or Y"). The
  posting wants the ask, and any one example meets it.
- **Each member keeps its own criterion and label.** A group changes no `requirement`:
  every member is labeled by the rules above.
- **"or other", "or similar", "or comparable" add nothing** — no extra skill, no broad
  parent.
- **Not alternatives:** skills asked for together ("X and Y", "X, Y and Z"), and a broad
  skill named alongside its examples. "cloud platforms (GCP, AWS or Azure)" groups `gcp`,
  `aws` and `azure`; `cloud` stays out of the group.
- **A group needs at least two skills.** A skill also asked for on its own elsewhere in the
  posting (including as an unmarked tech-stack entry) is a requirement on its own: it leaves
  the group.
- A Golden whose groups have been checked carries `groups_reviewed: true`. Only those
  Goldens are scored on grouping; the others are not scored on it at all.

This matches extraction rule 9 in `PRINCIPLES` (`app/extract.py`).
